# Independent review of ConstructibleOrder

**Clean/accept.** I read all 587 lines of `Computability/BusyBeaver/Lean/BusyBeaver/ZFC/ConstructibleOrder.lean` and the relevant preceding APIs in ConstructibleAbs, CodeOrder, TupleOrder, SatSupport, InternalWO, OrderRec, Constructible, ConstructibleDef and ConstructibleZF. I found no mathematical defect, improper class-size assumption, hidden object-level Choice, standard-code restriction or empty-field shortcut. This was a read-only source review: no Lean build or executable suite was run. The JSON identifies the exact sources and copied snapshots.

Reviewed HEAD is `28b0f7e26f08961d612afd17b029b67a46b05636`. The new source is byte-identical to commit `6c75f70e41`, SHA256 `399fabe52b0998e9ec41e7f9f21d819ef9ba11cb6ecc5f944ac59a81ac11dd74`, 587 lines/28,426 bytes. Snapshots are under `/tmp/zfc-constructible-order-review-sources`.

## Exact assumptions and internal meaning

The final statement is `choice_of_VL` at line 563, under H, hR, hP and hVL. H is the actual six-field `ZFAxioms` bundle (`SetTheory/ZF/Lean/ZF/Zf.lean:334`): Extensionality, formula-indexed Separation, Pairing, Union, Infinity and formula-indexed partial Replacement. Power and Regularity are separate explicit hypotheses. `hVL : ∀ x, InL H hP x` says every ambient object is internally constructible. There is no Choice, global choice function, externally well-founded membership relation, transitive standard model or standardness-of-omega hypothesis.

`InternalWO.IsWO` at lines 28–33 requires a least element only for each represented nonempty set contained in its field. It is not an assertion of external well-foundedness on all metatheoretic subsets. The same internal reading applies to `IsWOS` and every stage theorem. A countable externally ill-founded model is not silently replaced by a standard model.

## Keys really are bounded by one set

This is the critical size argument. `key_set` at lines 259–279 does not collect arbitrary chosen witnesses. Let CF represent the field of CW. It constructs

`T1 = omega × F`, `PT = Power(T1)`, `B1 = omega × PT`, `B = CF × B1`.

An IsKey unpacks as `k=pair(c,pair(n,t))`, with c in CF, n in internal omega and t an actual function graph on n whose values lie in F. `IsFunctionOn` has a no-junk clause: every member of t is a pair(i,y) with i in n. Since n is an internal natural, n is a subset of internal omega. Every such pair therefore belongs to T1, including when n is nonstandard externally. Thus t belongs to PT, and k belongs to B. The bound is independent of the represented set Z whose elements' keys are being selected.

The last operation is actual Separation on B using `exists y in Z, IsKey(...)`, represented by `isKeyF` and checked by `nsat_isKeyF`. Universal quantification over environments in Defines is part of a finite named formula, not an arbitrary external predicate supplied to Separation. All keys of the members of Z really form a represented set. This discharges the explicit `hset` hypothesis of `InternalWO.wo_pull:199–204`, which would otherwise be a genuine proper-class gap.

## Existence, uniqueness and the empty field

`Defines` at lines 34–36 requires that every represented membership relation/environment completing the tuple define the same subset. Its named formula at lines 56–79 uses fresh finite variable names and the actual environment-cons graph formula; functionality of the environment proves that the existential graph is exactly econs. The other key/order predicates have corresponding satisfaction lemmas, so later Separation/ordinal induction uses actual schema instances.

`key_exists:222` handles an empty subset by bottom plus the empty tuple. For a definable subset it starts from an actual membership relation, code and environment. That environment itself supplies a point of F. `SatSupport.sat_support` applies to every internally valid code, not only external quotations, through its literal named induction property. Restricting the environment to its internal finite support n gives an actual tuple. Every completion agrees on that tuple; `agreeP_econs` preserves this agreement after inserting the tested element, and support gives the same satisfaction value. Encoded membership relations are unique by Extensionality.

`key_unique:204` correctly assumes F nonempty. One default point extends any tuple to an environment on all internal omega, using a product/Separation construction. The common key has the same code, length and tuple by pair injectivity; applying both Defines witnesses to this common environment then gives equal subsets by Extensionality.

An unconditional version would be false because Defines may be vacuous on an empty carrier. The proof does **not** use one: `new_wo:287–291` explicitly branches on F's nonemptiness. If F is empty, every element of Gdef(F) is a subset of F and hence empty. Thus all new elements are equal by Extensionality, providing the needed restricted uniqueness without pretending that arbitrary empty-carrier keys determine arbitrary sets.

`key_wo:155` orders codes, internal lengths and same-length tuples lexicographically. CodeOrder's field may include additional pair-closed objects; IsKey retains the valid-code condition. Additional field objects do not harm well-ordering or completeness of keys. TupleOrder's least-element theorem is proved by an actual formula instance of internal omega induction, for all n in omega, with actual set bounds for prefixes and last values. No external finite enumeration of a nonstandard tuple is used.

## The step, recursion and stage fields

`setNew_exists:323`, `setOrd_exists:330` and `setGL_exists:359` use actual finite formulas and represented product/union bounds. The step retains the old order, adds all old-to-new pairs and orders the new set by least keys. `appendOpL:390` discharges the generic end-extension theorem's four resources, including new/old disjointness and the complete field restriction on the new relation.

The noncomputable choices select sets whose exact memberships are already proved, and the uniquely characterized code order. These are metatheoretic names for existing extensional objects, not an assumed object-level family choice principle. `inGLF` eliminates them from the recursion's graph formula: field objects are specified extensionally, and `codeOrder_unique` identifies any witness satisfying the literal code-order formula. Thus `stepLOp:503` really is a definable operation usable by TransRec.

`lord_wos:521` applies the previously proved internal end-extension recursion theorem. `lord_fld:525` supplies the actual named property for ordinal induction and compares both recursions at every internal ordinal. The stage convention is consistent on both sides: each stage is the union of the next-step images of its predecessors. An old field element remains in Def(Lc) because Lc is transitive and `mem_gdef_of_mem` applies; new elements are precisely the Def(Lc) elements outside Lc. Zero/successor/limit cases are not shifted by one. No external class recursion function is assumed.

Nonpair junk in the generic order-set representation is ignored by its Le/Fld interface. The final consumer only uses this checked interface; it does not assert a stronger literal-purity property of arbitrary order sets.

## Exact Choice conclusion

`ChoiceSem` is the official Zermelo selector formulation at `SetTheory/BoundedConsistency/Lean/BoundedZFCConsistency/Choice.lean:119`: every pairwise disjoint family of nonempty sets has a set meeting each member in exactly one point. Its exact sealed-form bridge already exists at line 168. The new theorem does not silently substitute a stronger global choice function.

For a family x, `choice_of_VL:563` bounds **all members of union(x)** in one L stage using the existing actual-form stage_bound theorem. The canonical order of that stage orders every candidate point. Actual Separation on union(x), with the finite formula at lines571–576, takes all least points of family members. Every nonempty member y has a least point by the internal well-order interface. If w is another point in y and the selector, its selector witness is some y' in x; the common point w and pairwise disjointness force y=y'. Both leastness inequalities and antisymmetry give w=m. The empty-family case needs no exception or arbitrary selected point.

## Concrete remaining adapter at this review's HEAD

The new file proves conditional Choice under V=L. At the reviewed HEAD it does not yet define the final constructible-ZFC model or finite-refutation comparison. Those are now small composition steps:

1. Apply `choice_of_VL` inside the actual subtype `{x // InL H hP x}`, using `ConstructibleZF.L_zfAxioms:313`, `L_regular:374`, `L_power:365` and `ConstructibleAbs.vEqL:987`. This gives `ChoiceSem (memL H hP)` with no remaining V=L premise.
2. Combine `ConstructibleZF.L_models_ZF:399` with `bridge_Choice_sealed.mpr` and split the two branches of `ZFCax_s:188`. This gives every sealed ZFC axiom under any explicit L valuation. An explicit inhabited valuation can use `natV H 0` with `ConstructibleAbs.inL_natV H hR hP 0`.
3. Given a ZFC refutation, apply `completeness_inf` to ZFax_s. From any ZF model obtain H, hP and hR via `ZFNative.models_ZF:34`, build its inhabited L model, and contradict the ZFC refutation using `soundness_BProv`. This yields a ZF refutation. `theory_transfer` is not directly the correct interface: it demands the same underlying carrier, whereas L is a subtype.
4. Compose with `BinaryPerm252.nonhalting_iff_zf_consistency:110` and the already checked opposite standard-theory implication to obtain the external Lean Con(ZFC) endpoint.

The existing ConstructibleAbs bridge is adequate: code_up/down cover internal codes by actual formula induction/least-rank arguments; arbitrary ambient environments can be replaced on their internal finite support by constructible ones; Gdef is absolute; the hierarchy comparison gives V=L in L. There is no new mathematical missing-Choice obstacle in that composition.

These are external model/provability metatheorems. Even after their Lean proofs are checked, they do not themselves construct an effective finite proof-code translation or prove its correctness/totality in PA. A direct internal PA or ZFC statement about the serialized machine still requires the separate arithmetic/trace comparison work. Nothing in this source review changes that boundary.

Post-review update: the separate `ChoiceCalibration254.lean` glue now implements all four external adapter steps above and has a successful scoped source/audit record. Its independent source review is `/tmp/zfc-choice-adapter/independent-review.md/json`. Thus the “remaining adapter at this review's HEAD” section is a historical frontier, not a current mathematical gap; only maintained integration and the separately identified internal arithmetic/proof-code work remain.
